en.title: First Player to Win k Games in a Row
en.description:
Players line up in their original order. The two players at the front compare their distinct potentials; the larger one wins and stays at the front, and the loser goes to the back. The process ends as soon as someone first wins k games in a row; output the winner's potential.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n k, followed by n distinct potentials. Original bounds: N/A. This site uses 2≤n≤200000, 1≤k≤10^18, and potentials are integers in −10^9..10^9; they are not required to be a permutation of 1..n.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; -2; 3. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Scan the original queue while maintaining the champion and its win streak, counting from 1 again whenever the champion changes; if the process has not ended when the scan finishes, return the global maximum potential.
